content:
Jess: Heads up — console charts (heatmap + sparklines) are stalling on canary after the routing-weight tweak. Seeing long main-thread frames. :eyes:
Rory: ugh, saw a spike in LCP/TotalBlockingTime in SLO graphs this morning, thought it was telemetry.
Jess: I profiled a user session — large JS parse + worker spin. Looks like worker pool allocations spike when kvcache misses happen.
Amit: hmm, routing-weight tweak also changed which CDN origin serves prefetch bundles. Could be extra bytes. Any network waterfall?
Jess: small increase in bundle size (~12kb) but CPU is the bigger hit. Worker heap grows then GC pauses.
Lucy: can you paste the flamegraph?
Jess: ```
MainThread -> parseScripts -> evaluate -> runMicrotasks -> Chart.render -> hydrate -> computeLayout
Worker(pool-3) -> parseCSV -> decompress -> postMessage -> main thread receive -> layout calc
```
Marco: that parseCSV step shouldn't be on worker for heatmap, it's usually streamed. Did the route change change payload shape?
Jess: payload shape changed — new field `perf_annotations` added by the rollout. For large queries it tacks on ~200kb.
Rory: rollout added annotations via internal /api/v1/query/response v2 right? We switched to passthrough earlier this week.
Amit: yep, routing policy sends canary traffic to v2 now. v2 includes telemetry annotations by default.
Lucy: if payload bigger, workers spin up to parse then send big messages back (postMessage cost). That matches the GC + main-thread stall pattern.
Rory: regression correlation: timestamp 6161600000 when routing-weight changed. Matches the canary rollout.
Marco: quick mitigation: strip perf_annotations server-side for console clients or make annotations optional behind a query param.
Jess: temporary patch: client checks `X-Client-Mode: console` and server returns slim payload. Can we hotfix?
Amit: we can gate with routing policy -> add header in routing config for console origin. But that requires a quick release to API layer, low risk.
Rory: also consider switching worker message passing to Transferable ArrayBuffer for big blobs to avoid copying. Longer fix.
Lucy: agree. Short term server-side slim payload + revert annotations for console should cut the allocs.
Marco: ops note — if we slim payload, we still need telemetry copies for infra. Could send annotations to telemetry pipeline async rather than in response body.
Jess: test plan: push header-gate to canary, verify reduced GC and frame times, then rollout. If OK, rev the client to use Transferables in next sprint.
deploy-bot: deploy requested by @Amit for service api-query on branch fix/slim-console-payload -> canary queue.
Amit: I pushed the header change and a toggle. Canaries green for 5m locally, starting canary.
Rory: monitoring checks: console LCP, TBT, and worker allocs. I'll add an alert for sudden postMessage payload > 100kb.
Lucy: I'll prepare a small benchmark reproducer (large query with annotations) and try transferable buffers patch.
Jess: thanks team. If canary looks good after 30m, let's promote and add follow-up Jira for Transferables + better chunking of annotations. :thumbsup:
Marco: FYI also filing a note for docs/console-api about `perf_annotations` — make it opt-in for UI clients.
Rory: one more thing — routing policy logs should include `client-type` so we can trace these behavior changes faster next time.
Amit: added to the rollout checklist.
Jess: ok closing thread once canary promoted. Will post numbers. :party:
